issueOrPullRequest.title: Planning loops: collapse each review loop's own commits into one commit per document
issueOrPullRequest.body:
Planning artifacts (slice design, task breakdown, etc.) accumulate a commit set per artifact: create, review, revise, and each loop iteration. Every review version is already archived in the files, so the intermediate commits add noise to \`git log\`. Each set should collapse to one commit.

Example: slice 400's design was 7 commits and its tasks 7 more. They were squashed by hand into "add slice 400 ... design" and "add slice 400 task breakdown".

## Proposal

A deterministic command (name open: \`sq docs squash\`, or a \`cf\` command, since cf owns document formats and phases). No LLM.

- **Set detection by file, not by commit subject.** A set is a run of consecutive commits that touch only one artifact file plus its review files. Subjects are labels and must not drive logic.
- **Survivor:** the set's first commit keeps its message. Later commits are folded in as fixups.
- **When:** at the end of a review loop (verdict PASS, or CONCERNS accepted), before the next phase starts. It always runs before anything is pushed.
- **Safety:**
  - Refuse if any commit in the run is already on the remote.
  - Tag a backup before rewriting.
  - Verify the final tree is identical to the pre-squash tree.
  - Preserve merge topology (use \`--rebase-merges\`), because slice-range resolution reads merge commits (slice 403).
  - Operate on the configured target (\`git.integration_branch\`, or \`main\`).
  - Require a clean working tree.

## Notes from the manual run

- \`git rebase\` only opens the sequence editor with \`-i\`. Without it, a scripted todo edit silently does nothing.
- The rebase todo format is \`pick <hash> # <subject>\`, and parsing it has to tolerate the \`# \`.
- Review-fix commits made after several designs were written together touch several sets. They need splitting per artifact before folding.

Pipeline integration is tracked separately.

nodes.body: sq squash was removed in 0.24.12. Kept open for the replacement: a review loop records HEAD when it starts and the shas of its own round commits, and when it finishes collapses them (plus the phase step's commit) into one commit per document. It only collapses commits it can prove it made; anything else in between leaves history alone with a one-line warning. Per-round commits still exist during the loop, so the findings-addressed gate keeps its prior-round base.

Shipped in slice 202 (0.24.13): planning loops record their own round commits (loop_ledger.py) and collapse them, plus the phase step's commit, into one commit per document on completion (loop_collapse.py). Foreign commits in between leave history alone with a warning. Resolving review notes inside the loop is #287.
